svg.title: Drawing a vector as an arrow
svg.desc: Three velocity vectors drawn as arrows from a single common point. One points right, labelled 6.0 metres per second; one points straight up, labelled 3.0 metres per second; one points down and to the left, labelled 4.5 metres per second. Each arrow points in the direction of its velocity, and the arrows are drawn to one scale, so the 3.0 arrow is exactly half the length of the 6.0 arrow and the 4.5 arrow is three quarters of it. Length carries the magnitude and nothing else: a longer arrow is a larger velocity, not a different kind of quantity. Illustrative data.
svg.text: drawn to one scale: 6.0 m/s is the longest arrow
Direction is where it points; length is proportional to magnitude
One scale for all three: half the magnitude is half the length.
